Practical AI

Treat AI like a smart intern

Fast, well-read, eager to help, and brand new to your business. Manage it the way you'd manage a new hire and the work gets better.

Tap play. Sound plays only when you choose.

STAGE 1 OF 5

Meet your intern

It has read more than any person could and writes in seconds. It never gets tired and never says "that's not my job."

It knows nothing about your clients, your prices or last week's meeting unless you tell it.

Your guide: Bradley RossInstructor. Builds and runs AI agents in production.

STAGE 2 OF 5

Give it a proper brief

A one-line request gets a generic answer. Tell it who to be, who it's for, what good looks like and any limits.

Example

Write a follow-up email.

The intern has to guess the client, the tone and the goal.

Example

You're my account manager. Write a follow-up to Dana, a client who asked for a spring quote. Friendly, under 120 words. End by offering two call times.

Role, reader, tone, length and the next step. Nothing left to guess.

STAGE 3 OF 5

Expect confident mistakes

Your intern sounds just as sure when it's wrong as when it's right. When it doesn't know, it often fills the gap with something that only looks correct.

Look closer at the glowing scroll. It looks official, but the writing is nonsense. AI output can work the same way. Check every name, number, date and quote before it leaves your desk.
STAGE 4 OF 5

Coach it instead of redoing it

When a draft misses, say what to change: "shorter," "warmer," "use our pricing." A good intern gets better with specific feedback. So does AI.

Same truth, different script. You bring judgment and context. It brings speed. The work is best when both hands are on the page.
STAGE 5 OF 5

Delegate the work, keep the decision

The intern drafts

  • First drafts
  • Summaries
  • Research to check
  • Options to choose from

You decide

  • Anything sent
  • Anything signed
  • Anything paid
  • Anything published

Every workflow needs one point where a person reviews and says yes.

YOUR NEXT STEP

Launch

Pick one task you repeat every week and hand it to your intern.

  1. Write the brief: role, reader, goal, limits.
  2. Read the draft and check the facts.
  3. Give one round of specific feedback.
  4. Make the final call yourself.

Check yourself

Why did the vague email prompt fail?

The intern had to guess the client, the tone and the goal. A brief removes the guessing.

The AI cites a statistic you've never seen. What now?

Treat it like an intern's claim: find the source before you use it. Confident wording is not proof.

Which step should AI never do alone?

The final decision: sending, signing, paying or publishing. A person says yes.

A smart intern needs a clear brief, a careful review and a manager who makes the call. So does AI.
